capabilities: Open .tex files as rendered notes with Obsidian's renderer and theme
Edit LaTeX in place with live preview, source, and reading modes
Resolve cross-references, citations from .bib files, macros, and counters
Render figures, tables, theorems, and TikZ diagrams (via a TikZ plugin)
Create new .tex documents from a configurable template
disambiguation: Not a math-in-Markdown editor or a LaTeX compiler; it opens existing .tex files as notes and never produces PDFs.
extras: Code was written by an AI model (Anthropic's Claude) directed by the maintainer; the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff; beta versions are installable via BRAT; the README details security measures (no network access, untrusted-document escaping) and lists explicit limitations such as .tex files not being indexed by search, backlinks, or graph.
problem: Obsidian cannot open or render .tex files, so LaTeX documents stay outside the vault workflow unless a separate TeX toolchain is used.

relations.evidence: drawn when a plugin that renders tikz code blocks is installed, such as TikZJax Next

summary: Opens .tex files as rendered, editable Obsidian notes by converting LaTeX to markdown in memory, with no TeX installation and no PDF output.
